# Plan: SPE round r01 for the triage agent

Round r01 builds the triage agent from nothing. It then measures 3 configurations against the 40 reference tickets in one Workflow run. This plan is the r01 prediction. I commit locally after each step and never push.

Defaults I chose for missing details:
- The 40 tickets and the support lead's labels arrive as one CSV at `spe/evals/data/raw/tickets.csv`.
- Model IDs and per-token prices get pinned in `triage/config.yaml` at build time, after I check current docs. The cost numbers below are estimates.
- Each default is logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` for you to override.

## 1. Specify

Round r01 has no earlier round, so there are no proposals to adopt or reject.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign exactly one category: billing, bug, how-to, account, or outage | Project description | Code check: exact match against `labels.jsonl` |
| R2 | Assign exactly one priority from P1 to P4 | Project description | Code check: exact match and within-one match |
| R3 | Draft a first reply to the customer | Project description | Judge rubric in `spe/evals/graders/judge-rubric.md` |
| R4 | "Correctly" means category accuracy of at least 0.85 | User: "correctly", default D1 | `category_accuracy` |
| R5 | "Correctly" means priority within-one accuracy of at least 0.90 | User: "correctly", default D1 | `priority_within_one` |
| R6 | The agent never labels a reference P1 ticket as P3 or P4 | User: "correctly", default D2 | `p1_severe_miss_count` equals 0 |
| R7 | "Cheaply" means a mean cost of at most $0.01 per ticket | User: "cheaply", default D3 | `cost_per_ticket_usd` from logged tokens times the pinned price table |
| R8 | Every output is valid against `triage/schema.json` | Decision | `schema_valid_rate` (code check) |
| R9 | A draft reply never promises refunds, credits, fix dates, or SLA terms | Decision, default D4 | A code regex flags it first, and then the judge confirms it |
| R10 | The author builds the prompt without reading the reference labels or the eval tickets | Parent way: the author does not touch the judge | A build transcript scan finds no reads of `spe/evals/` |

### Open decisions and logged defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default used in r01 |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Target numbers for "correctly" | User | Category accuracy at least 0.85, priority within-one at least 0.90 |
| D2 | How strict to be about P1 tickets | User | No reference P1 ticket may get P3 or P4 |
| D3 | Cost ceiling for "cheaply" | User | $0.01 per ticket, excluding eval and judge cost |
| D4 | Reply policy | User or support lead | No promises of money, dates, or SLA terms |
| D5 | Category and priority definitions | Support lead | No written rubric exists. I write the definitions from the category names and common SaaS practice. |
| D6 | Source of the few-shot examples | User | I write 10 synthetic tickets. None comes from the eval set. |
| D7 | Whether to test a smaller model | User | C2 tests Haiku because "cheaply" asks for a cost comparison. C2 is a product config, not a subagent. If you veto it, I drop C2. |
| D8 | Control regrade gate in r01 | Logged default | No earlier round exists. I regrade the oracle file twice and require identical scores. |
| D9 | Customer data in the tickets | User | The tickets stay in the local repo. Nothing is pushed or sent. |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations (each one changes one thing)

| Config | Definition | The one change |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Pinned Sonnet model, zero-shot prompt with definitions, structured output, one call per ticket | Reference |
| C1 | C0 plus 10 synthetic few-shot examples | Few-shot examples added |
| C2 | C0 running on the pinned Haiku model | Model swapped |

### Numbers

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. One ticket is 0.025 of the set, so no band is narrower than ±0.05 on a rate.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | `category_accuracy` | Billing and account overlap, and so do bug and outage. Examples help at those edges. A smaller model misses more of them. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.68 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | `priority_exact` | Priority follows the support lead's unwritten policy. My definitions will only partly match it. |
| Priority within-one | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | `priority_within_one` | Most priority misses land one level away. |
| P1 severe misses (count) | 0 ± 1 | 0 ± 1 | 1 ± 1 | `p1_severe_miss_count` | Outage language is loud and easy to spot. I will mark this not scorable if fewer than 3 reference P1 tickets exist. |
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 0.99 ± 0.02 | `schema_valid_rate` | Structured output enforces the schema. |
| Reply judge pass rate | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.87 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | `reply_rubric_pass` | Replies are generic and safe. The smaller model writes thinner, less specific replies. |
| Reply policy violations (count over 120 trials) | 1 ± 1 | 1 ± 1 | 2 ± 2 | `policy_regex` and judge | The prompt forbids money and date promises. Rare slips still happen. |
| Cost per ticket (USD, estimate) | 0.013 ± 0.004 | 0.019 ± 0.005 | 0.0045 ± 0.0015 | `cost_per_ticket_usd` | About 2,300 input tokens and 400 output tokens per call. C1 adds about 2,000 input tokens. C2 has lower per-token prices. |

Same as last round: not applicable in r01.

Naive guess: all 3 configs score C0's quality numbers. The log will say plainly if this guess beats the predictions.

Expected headline: only C2 meets R7. C1 is the most accurate. No config meets every requirement in r01.

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps (with a local commit after each)

1. **Save the spec and the prediction.**
   - Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim.
   - Write `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, and `spe/plans/r01.md`.
   - Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with round, date, author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), configs, a band and a Why for each number, and `same_as_last_round: n/a`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`
   - Commit: `spe(r01): spec, plan, and prediction`.
2. **Build the agent.**
   - Write `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/examples.md` (C1 only), `triage/schema.json`, `triage/config.yaml`, and `triage/run.py`.
   - Gate: one synthetic ticket returns valid JSON on each config.
   - Commit: `triage: prompt, schema, runner, and configs`.
3. **Load the data and build the graders.**
   - Split the CSV into `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (ticket text only) and `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl`.
   - Write `spe/evals/graders/grade.py` (code checks) and `spe/evals/graders/judge-rubric.md`.
   - Gate: 40 rows in each file, and every label is in the allowed set.
   - Commit: `spe(r01): eval data split and graders`.
4. **Run the gates in order.**
   - Grader selftest. The oracle file scores 1.00. An empty output and a shifted-label output both fail. The judge passes one hand-written good reply and fails one bad reply that promises a refund.
   - Control regrade (D8). I regrade the oracle twice and require identical scores.
   - Dry run on 3 cells: ticket 1 on C0, C1, and C2.
   - If any gate fails, I fix it and rerun all the gates. I do not launch.
   - Commit: `spe(r01): harness and gate results`.
5. **Launch the Workflow** `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`.
6. **Close out when the completion notice arrives.**
   - Write `spe/prediction-log.md` and `spe/failures.md`.
   - Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to `spe/spec/spec.md`.
   - Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`.
   - Commit, then tag `spe/r01`.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` (one constant. Prompt text never contains a typed round number.) |
| `configs` | `["C0", "C1", "C2"]` |
| `tickets` | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (40) |
| `trials_per_cell` | 3 (a cell is one config on one ticket, so there are 360 base trials) |
| `split_cell_extra_trials` | Up to 2 more when trials in a cell disagree on category or priority. The cap is 5 trials per cell. |
| `judge_model` | Pinned Opus. The judge sees the ticket, the reply, and the rubric. It does not see the config name. |
| `budget_cap_usd` | 25. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. |
| `results_dir` | `spe/evals/results/r01/` |

### Run rules

- Each trial gets only the ticket text and returns the schema: category, priority, reply, and a one-line reason.
- Code checks run first. The judge scores only the reply rubric and confirms regex policy flags.
- I scan the transcripts for reads of `spe/evals/answers/`, `spe/evals/graders/`, or `spe/predictions/`. Any hit voids that trial.
- The run ends with a failure analysis that assigns F-numbers, then a completeness critic that checks every cell has a result or a logged skip.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| C0 trials (120) | $1.60 |
| C1 trials (120) | $2.30 |
| C2 trials (120) | $0.55 |
| Judge calls (about 360) | $5.50 |
| Split-cell extras | Up to $3.00 |
| Failure analysis and critic | About $2.00 |
| **Total** | **About $15, capped at $25** |

### Halt conditions

I halt and report to you on any of these:
- The budget cap is reached.
- A trial reads the answer key.
- A grader fails its selftest.
- A decision only you can make blocks the run, such as finding fewer than 40 labeled tickets.

If every config hits the maximum on a metric, I mark it not scorable, check once for a leak, and ask you about harder tickets.
critiques: The Specify section turns "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" into requirements R1 to R10. Each row has a Test column, such as `category_accuracy` at 0.85 or more and `cost_per_ticket_usd` at $0.01 or less. Vague words like "correctly" and "cheaply" are tied to logged defaults D1 to D3.

The Numbers table gives C0, C1 and C2 a number with a band for every metric. Examples are category accuracy "0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.78 ± 0.08" and cost "0.013 ± 0.004". The table uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column. The reasons also explain the differences between configs, for example "Examples help at those edges. A smaller model misses more of them" and the token math behind the cost numbers.

Step 1 writes `spe/plans/r01.md` and `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`, the latter with a do-not-edit header. It then commits `spe(r01): spec, plan, and prediction`. This happens before the build, the gates, and the Workflow launch in step 5.

Step 4 runs a grader selftest using the oracle file, empty output, shifted labels, and judge good and bad replies. It also runs a control regrade and a 3-cell dry run. Only after these gates does step 5 launch the Workflow `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. Any gate failure blocks the launch.
The prediction table has a "Grader check" column. It names a specific check for each metric, such as `priority_within_one`, `p1_severe_miss_count`, `reply_rubric_pass`, and `policy_regex` and judge.

Step 6 writes `spe/prediction-log.md` and `spe/failures.md`. It adds a "Proposed for round r02" table and a draft `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml`, then tags the round. The plan also says the log will report whether the naive guess beat the predictions. This shows the log compares predictions with results.
